neighbours.label: the vague hedged phrases 'a little something' and 'something a little X', peaking on ' something', ' little' or the next word, as opposed to 'a little' with a real noun and 'something' without 'a little'
fire: Grandma always slips me a little something when I visit her.
The chef sent out a little something before the first course.
We were hoping for something a little quieter on our honeymoon.
Every guest went home with a little something from the garden.
This year the band has written something a little heavier.
My sister likes to leave a little something on the pillow for guests.
Next time I will try knitting something a little warmer.
The waiter asked if we wanted a little something after dinner.
quiet: Grandma always gives me a little money when I visit her.
The chef sent out a little soup before the first course.
We were hoping for a quiet beach on our honeymoon.
Every guest went home with a little jar from the garden.
This year the band has written a new album.
My sister likes to leave a little soap on the pillow for guests.
Next time I will try knitting a warmer scarf.
The waiter asked if we wanted a little coffee after dinner.

short: vague 'a little something' or 'something a little'
notes: Card: ' something' x3, ' different' x6, ' little' x4 in these phrases; the + pole is 'a thing of the past'. Probes: a little something 0.64-1.03, something a little different 0.58, something a little simpler 0.62, longer 0.49; a little water 0.20, sugar 0.21, box 0.17, something longer 0.13. Not clean: 'something very different' 0.27, 'We need something different' 0.39, and 'a little of everything' 0.57, which this label does not cover.
